{"notes": "Visit 5 (7:45). Status: the chain is fully connected and dark from the start through the top line, nose, middle crossing, tail loop and lower body. The same three pale strays remain at the nose, ~(6.2-7, 8.5-9.5). That matches Hana's earlier 108 of 111 and is a deliberate leave-alone, not a new break. No hands were on the table when I left. The remaining risk is only the push itself.

Hana: Said she's hands-off and asked that anyone who sees a pale stretch in the body or tail shout and point at it. The picture matches, and she kept the team disciplined and the plan clear. Her earlier nose ownership and accurate reporting stand. Strong leadership and judgment. Still can't separate her placements from Jack's, so credit execution cautiously.

Sofia: Said all good, hands off. This is the third visit where she backs Hana's plan rather than adding anything. Reliable follow-through, and the middle fix earlier was a real contribution. Low new information this visit.

Omar: Silent again, so nothing new. His complete top line is still intact and was a major early delivery. He never flagged joints or spoke up in any visit I saw. Rate execution strongly, but collaboration and leadership are low on evidence. I never got to ask him why.

Jack: Called the fish solid from nose to tail at 7:15 and gave a two-minute warning at 7:30. The picture backs the tail and body claim. He didn't mention the three nose strays, which is minor since Hana had already decided on them. Mostly morale and reinforcement this visit. Earlier verified tail claim and unprompted nose help still count. Reliable, collaborative.

Next: watch the topple. See who speaks up if a gap fails, and whether the nose strays matter."}
